entity.definition: A graph is said to be acyclic if it contains no cycle.
A graph G is bipartite if it is possible to partition the set of vertices of G into two subsets A and B such that every edge of G joins a vertex of A to a vertex of B.
The chromatic number of a graph G is the minimum number of different colors required to color the vertices of G such that two adjacent vertices have different colors.
The clique number of a graph G is the maximum cardinality of a clique in G.
A graph G is connected if every pair of vertices in G are joined by a path.
The diameter D of a graph G=(V,E) is the maximum distance between two vertices of G, i.e. the "longest shortest path" in G.
The edge connectivity of a graph G is the smallest number of edges of G whose deletion will cause G to not be connected.
The girth of G is the length of the shortest cycle (if any) in G.
The maximum degree of a graph G=(V,E) is the maximum value amongst all the degrees of its vertices.
The matching number of a graph G is the maximum cardinality of the maximal matchings of G.
The minimum degree of a graph G=(V,E) is the minimum value amongst all the degrees of its vertices.
Let G = (V,E) be a graph. The eccentricity of a vertex v in V is the maximum distance between v and any other vertex in V. The radius of G is the minimum eccentricity of its vertices.
A graph is said to be regular if all of the degrees of its vertices are equals.
The (edge) chromatic index of a graph G is the minimum number of different colors required to color the edges of G such that two edges incident to the same vertex have different colors.
The index or spectral radius of a graph is the greatest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

The Laplacian largest eigenvalue of a graph G is the largest eigenvalue of its Laplacian matrix L, defined by L = D - A where A is the adjacency matrix of G and D is a diagonal matrix where Di,i is the degree of vertex i.
The average degree of a graph G is the (arithmetic) mean of the degrees of its vertices.
The number of edges m of a graph G=(V,E), or its size, is the cardinal of E.

The algebraic connectivity of a graph G is the second smallest eigenvalue of its Laplacian matrix L, defined by L = D - A where A is the adjacency matrix of G and D is a diagonal matrix where Di,i is the degree of vertex i.
The second largest eigenvalue of a graph is the second largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.
The smallest eigenvalue of a graph is the smallest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.
The number of components of the graph.
The number of triangles of the graph.
A graph is Eulerian if it contains an Eulerian circuit. An Eulerian circuit is a closed walk which visits each edge of the graph exactly once.
A graph is Hamiltonian if it contains a Hamiltonian cycle. A Hamiltonian cycle is a cycle which contains every vertex of the graph.
The vertex connectivity of a graph G is the smallest number of vertices of G whose deletion will cause G to be disconnected.
A graph is Claw-Free if it does not contain a K_{1,3} as an induced subgraph.

The genus of a graph is the minimal integer n such that the graph can be drawn without crossing itself on a sphere with n handles (i.e. an oriented surface of genus n). Thus, a planar graph has genus 0, because it can be drawn on a sphere without self-crossing.
The density of a graph G = (V,E) is the number of edges divided by the largest possible number of edges of the graph (i.e. |V|*(|V|-1)/2).
The circumference of a graph is the order of the largest subgraph of the graph that is a cyclic graph.
A graph is Planar if it can be drawn in the plane without crossing edges.
The group size of a graph G is the size of the automorphism group of G, i.e. |Aut(G)|.
The number of orbits of the vertices of graph G under the action of its automorphism group Aut(G).
The number of vertices n of a graph G=(V,E), or its order, is the cardinality of V.
The order of the largest induced subgraph of the graph that is a cycle.
The number of edges of the longest induced path of the graph.

Tree treewidth of a graph G is the minimum width among all possible tree decompositions of G. A tree decomposition is a tree T such that every vertex x in V(T) has an associated bag B(x) that is a subset of V(G). Every edge e in E(G) must be a subset of at least one bag B(x). Moreover, for every vertex v in V(G), the set of tree vertices whose bags contain v induce a connected subtree of T. The width of a tree decomposition is the size of its largest bag minus one.
A graph is traceable if it contains a Hamiltonian path. A Hamiltonian path is a path which contains every vertex of the graph.
A graph G is hypotraceable if G is non-traceable and G-v is traceable for every vertex v of G.
A graph G is hypohamiltonian if G is non-hamiltonian and G-v is hamiltonian for every vertex v of G.
The number of spanning trees of a graph. A spanning tree of a graph is a subgraph that is a tree and which contains all vertices of that graph and some (or all) of the edges.
The number of eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of the graph that are equal to zero.

The vertex cover number of a graph is the size of a minimum vertex cover in that graph (i.e., a vertex cover of smallest possible size). A vertex cover of a graph G is a set S of vertices of G such that every edge of G has at least one of member of S as an endpoint.

The feedback vertex set number of a graph is the size of a smallest feedback vertex set. A feedback vertex set of a graph is a set of vertices whose removal leaves a graph without cycles (i.e., produces a forest).
The number of edges of the longest path of the graph.
The degeneracy of a graph G is the smallest integer k such that each subgraph of G contains a vertex of degree at most k.
The number of orbits of the edges of graph G under the action of its automorphism group Aut(G).
The number of orbits of the arcs (i.e. directed edges or flags) of graph G under the action of its automorphism group Aut(G).
A graph is Twin-Free if none of its vertices have the same (open) neighbourhood (i.e., twins cannot be adjacent).
The domination number of a graph G is the minimum cardinality of a set of vertices such that every vertex is either in the set or is a neighbour of a vertex in the set.
The independence number of a graph G is the maximum cardinality of an independent set in G. (A set of vertices is independent if no vertices of the set are adjacent).

The independent domination number of a graph G is the minimum cardinality of an independent dominating set. An independent dominating set is a set of vertices that is both dominating (i.e., every vertex is either in the set or is a neighbour of a vertex in the set) and independent (i.e., no vertices of the set are adjacent).
